Seneca highly aligned with recommendations from the scientific literature, with 
short lessons and a high quantity of questions; it is likely that Seneca increases 
student engagement and cognitive load by providing high level questions. 
Seneca did not seem offer an alternative to reading the provided slides, 
however, the quantity of reading was significantly less than Bitesize, which the 
author found more engaging. Seneca keeping track of failed questions could also 
be highly effective of ensuring students have actionable analytics to improve 
their learning outcomes. 
2.5.3  Cognito 
Cognito was a YouTube channel focusing on the sciences and mathematics; and 
they have expanded and now have a website (Cognito, 2024). 
The lesson on Cognito seem to take around 12-to-15-minuites to complete and 
begin with a video and are followed by questions. The video was relatively slow 
taking around 6 minutes to complete and was narrated at slow pace, reducing 
engagement. However, they were broken up into chapters or segments for each 
stage. The site uses gamified elements such as XP and streaks to increase user 
retention, and actionable analytics that would enable students to spot areas of 
low performance. 
The questions were typically high level and were of varying types limiting 
monotony. However, some more complex questions such as written answers 
required students to mark themselves, this is better than not having written 
answers at all, but students maybe bias in there marking.
